## Catalog Description

Engineering Data Analysis. (3-0). Credit 3. Selected topics in probability and data analysis for quality in engineering problems; measurement principles, data collection and data analysis to solve quality engineering problems; introduction to courses in the assurance sciences-reliability, maintainability, quality control and robust design.

## Course Learning Outcomes

At the end of this course, students should be able to

- (1) Learn the basic techniques of statistical learning and predictive modeling;

- (2) Learn the principles of building and validating modern statistical models for engineering applications;

- (3) Demonstrate your knowledge by implementing existing techniques, developing new techniques to solve real-world problems, and conducting a comprehensive and insightful review study on any emerging area of statistical learning and data mining.

## Grading Policy

Grades assigned are: A for 90% - 100%, B for 80% - 89.9%, C for 70% - 79.9%, D for 60% - 69.9%, F for below 60%.

Any disagreements regarding a grade received on any graded material must be discussed within two business days from posting of the grades. No grade will be changed beyond the two business days limit. Grades will be maintained in the gradebook within Canvas.

Homework is an important element of this course and should be performed individually. Sharing of work in any manner is a violation of academic integrity. Homework are supposed to be independent work, and use of solutions from websites or other resources are prohibited. Late submission of homework is strictly not allowed and the link to submit your work will promptly be unavailable after the scheduled due date. The course assessment will be based on

- 30% Homework

- 35% Midterm Exam

- 35% Final Project

## Late Work Policy

Work submitted by a student as makeup work for an excused absence is not considered late work and is exempt from the late work policy (Student Rule 7).
